claims.assertion: The driver cancelled the trip at 13:05:40, 7 min 40 s after accepting at 12:58:00, and the platform recorded a $6.61 cancellation fee against the rider on a RydeX trip covered by the cancellation policy.

The no-show cancellation fee can only stand if the driver pressed "I'm Here", was inside the pickup radius at that moment and waited inside it for more than 3 minutes; the timeline shows the "I'm Here" tap at 13:02:45 and only 2 min 55 s within 200 m of the pickup after the tap, so the over-3-minute waiting element is not met (≥ 3:01 required).

Measured from the platform's recorded arrival at 13:01:10, the driver had waited 4 min 30 s at cancellation, but the GPS shows he was not at the pickup point for the first stretch: his stationary spell at 40 m from the pickup did not begin until 13:02:25 and lasted 3 min 15 s up to the moment of cancellation.

Because the NS-1 preconditions (driver's proximity/"I'm Here" and waiting in excess of 3 minutes per the system records) are not satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full to the rider.

The driver's written statement claims he pressed "I'm Here" and waited more than 3 minutes, but the driver's own timeline entry is internally contradicted by the GPS within-200 m duration of 2 min 55 s after his tap; the system records govern over the statement.
The driver's chat at 13:05 asserting he "waited more than 3 min" is a statement conflict with the system's measured wait after the "I'm Here" tap, so the statement cannot establish the fee.

The rider is a 3.9-year account with a 4.81 rating and zero disputes or upheld complaints in the last 90 days, which supports her account that she was on her way out when the driver cancelled a minute later.
The driver has a clean record (0 disputes, 0 upheld in 90 days, 651 trips), so no account flag is appropriate here; the rider seeks only the return of the fee, not any action against the driver.
Traffic on Tampines Street 82 was band 3 (20–29 km/h) with no incidents and fair weather, so no operational condition explains away the imposed fee or the rider's one-minute delay.

weaknesses: The driver recorded arrival at 13:01:10 and cancelled at 13:05:40 (F5) and was within 200 m for a cumulative 4 min 30 s (F2), so the other side will argue he waited way past 3 minutes and that the post-tap window is not the right measuring point under NS-1(iii).

The driver's chat and statement both assert he pressed "I'm Here" and waited over 3 minutes (F11, F12), which superficially satisfies the narrative in NS-1; the rider's case depends on the stricter reading of the GPS within-200 m post-tap duration (F6).

The rider's complaint admits she only came out "a minute after the driver cancelled", i.e. she was not at the pickup point during the waiting window at all, which supports the driver's no-show narrative (F4, F6).

The driver's GPS shows him stationary 40 m from the pickup from 13:02:25 to 13:05:40 (F3), a strong indication he really was at the pickup point, and his profile is clean (F17), so a judge may read the wait requirement leniently.

claims.assertion: The driver accepted the RydeX trip at 12:58:00 and cancelled at 13:05:40, and the $6.61 cancellation fee was charged on the basis that the rider failed to show at the pickup point.

The GPS record shows the driver did reach the pickup point: closest approach 38 m at 13:04:30, first within 200 m at 13:01:10, satisfying the 'at the pick-up location according to GPS data' element of NS-1 (ii).
Before cancelling, the driver was stationary for 3 min 15 s (13:02:25–13:05:40) just 40 m from the pickup point, i.e. he waited at the pickup point for more than 3 minutes as NS-1 (iii) requires.

Platform records show the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 13:02:45 while 41 m from the pickup point, and he then remained within 200 m for the following 2 min 55 s until cancellation, so the NS-1 (i) arrival indication is satisfied and corroborated by GPS.

The rider did not board during the waiting period: the driver's message at 13:02 announced arrival and his 13:05 message confirms 'Waited more than 3 min, cancelling', consistent with the rider's own account that she only came out after the cancellation.

The rider's excuse that traffic or road conditions prevented her from coming out is unsupported: no traffic incidents were recorded near the route during the trip window, the only congestion was band 3 (20–29 km/h) on Tampines Street 82, and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain.

The driver's account corroborates the fee: he states he pressed 'I'm Here' and waited more than 3 minutes before cancelling for rider no-show, and his 90-day history is clean (0 disputes, 0 upheld, rating 4.9 over 651 trips), which weighs against any suggestion that the cancellation was opportunistic.
The $6.61 cancellation fee is therefore valid and should stand unchanged; the driver's entitlement under the published policy is the $4.50 share of that fee.

weaknesses: The rider can rely on F5 and F7: F7 states the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' (driver_pressed_here_at is null), which directly contradicts the timeline fact F6 that records a tap at 13:02:45 — if the judge reads F7 as the controlling system record, NS-1 (i) fails and the fee would have to be refunded under NS-2.

F6 itself shows the driver stayed within 200 m for only 2 min 55 s after tapping 'I'm Here', and F2 gives cumulative time within 200 m as 4 min 30 s counting from 13:01:10 rather than from the tap; the rider can argue that the '>3 minutes waiting' in NS-1 (iii) should be measured from the arrival indication, which would put the wait at 2:55 and defeat NS-1 (iii).

The rider's statement that she 'came out a minute after the driver cancelled' cannot be checked against any system field in the fact table, and the $6.61 fee was charged to the rider rather than collected by the driver, so the driver has no monetary claim of his own here — the best available outcome is simply that no refund is ordered.

The driver's own chat messages (F10, F11) are user-submitted content and lose to system records where they conflict; they add nothing to the GPS/timeline proof of waiting and cannot cure the F6/F7 contradiction.

events.body:
→ D1 (concedes): Conceded as to the bare sequence: acceptance at 12:58:00 and driver cancellation at 13:05:40 with a $6.61 fee on record (F4, F8) is common ground under NS-0 — what is disputed is only whether NS-1's preconditions are met. [F4 F8] [NS-0]
→ D2: Proximity alone is not enough: NS-1 (ii) requires the driver to be within the pickup radius at the moment of the arrival indication, and NS-1 (i)/(iii) must also be satisfied by the same system record — a 38 m closest approach at 13:04:30 (F1, F2) proves presence, not the tap-plus-wait combination. [F1 F2] [NS-1]
→ D3: The 13:02:25–13:05:40 stationary spell of 3 min 15 s (F3) starts 1 min 15 s after the recorded 13:01:10 arrival (F5), so counting from the earliest point the driver was at the pickup the wait is 4 min 30 s, but counting from the "I'm Here" tap NS-1 (i) requires it is only 2 min 55 s (F6) — short of the ≥ 3:01 required. [F3 F5 F6] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D4: F6 is contradicted by F7, which records driver_pressed_here_at as null (the driver never tapped "I'm Here"); on my own case I accept the stricter reading that the post-tap window is only 2 min 55 s, so NS-1 (i) and (iii) fail and NS-2 requires full refund. [F6 F7] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D5: It is agreed the rider boarded after the cancellation (F1 shows the closest approach was 38 m and no pickup occurred), but none of that cures the unmet NS-1 preconditions; the rider's non-boarding is not itself one of the three conditions the policy requires before a fee can stand. [F1 F6] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D6 (concedes): Conceded: no traffic incident was recorded near the route, only band 3 (20–29 km/h) on Tampines Street 82, and weather was fair (F13, F14, F15); the rider's case does not rest on traffic or weather but on the fee's conditions under NS-1. [F13 F14 F15] [NS-1]
→ D7: The driver's statement (F12) is user-submitted content and loses to the system records that show only 2 min 55 s within 200 m after the tap (F6) and a null tap field (F7), and his clean 90-day record (F17) cannot substitute for the missing NS-1 element. [F12 F6 F7 F17] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D8: Because NS-1 (i) and (iii) are not established on the system records, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 charged (F8) must be refunded in full, and the driver's $4.50 share is contingent on a fee that never validly arose. [F8 F6 F7] [NS-2]

points.response: Conceded as to the bare sequence: acceptance at 12:58:00 and driver cancellation at 13:05:40 with a $6.61 fee on record (F4, F8) is common ground under NS-0 — what is disputed is only whether NS-1's preconditions are met.

Proximity alone is not enough: NS-1 (ii) requires the driver to be within the pickup radius at the moment of the arrival indication, and NS-1 (i)/(iii) must also be satisfied by the same system record — a 38 m closest approach at 13:04:30 (F1, F2) proves presence, not the tap-plus-wait combination.

The 13:02:25–13:05:40 stationary spell of 3 min 15 s (F3) starts 1 min 15 s after the recorded 13:01:10 arrival (F5), so counting from the earliest point the driver was at the pickup the wait is 4 min 30 s, but counting from the "I'm Here" tap NS-1 (i) requires it is only 2 min 55 s (F6) — short of the ≥ 3:01 required.

F6 is contradicted by F7, which records driver_pressed_here_at as null (the driver never tapped "I'm Here"); on my own case I accept the stricter reading that the post-tap window is only 2 min 55 s, so NS-1 (i) and (iii) fail and NS-2 requires full refund.

It is agreed the rider boarded after the cancellation (F1 shows the closest approach was 38 m and no pickup occurred), but none of that cures the unmet NS-1 preconditions; the rider's non-boarding is not itself one of the three conditions the policy requires before a fee can stand.

Conceded: no traffic incident was recorded near the route, only band 3 (20–29 km/h) on Tampines Street 82, and weather was fair (F13, F14, F15); the rider's case does not rest on traffic or weather but on the fee's conditions under NS-1.

The driver's statement (F12) is user-submitted content and loses to the system records that show only 2 min 55 s within 200 m after the tap (F6) and a null tap field (F7), and his clean 90-day record (F17) cannot substitute for the missing NS-1 element.

Because NS-1 (i) and (iii) are not established on the system records, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 charged (F8) must be refunded in full, and the driver's $4.50 share is contingent on a fee that never validly arose.

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.85)
events.body:
The trip was a RydeX booking accepted 12:58:00 and cancelled by the driver at 13:05:40, with a $6.61 cancellation fee on record, so the case falls into the driver-cancellation / rider-no-show branch of NS-0 and the fee stands only if NS-1 (i)–(iii) are all satisfied [F4][F8][NS-0].

NS-1 (i) is met on the platform record: the execution trace and the timeline show an "I'm Here" tap at 13:02:45, and the GPS-tagged tap position of 41 m from the pickup (closest approach 38 m at 13:04:30) satisfies NS-1 (ii) proximity at the moment of the tap [F6][F1][NS-1]. The rider's reliance on F7 (driver_pressed_here_at null) cannot remove this, because the timeline/arrival records (F5, F6) are the system records and the policy requires only that arrival be indicated and GPS-verified [F5][F6][NS-1].

The decisive element is NS-1 (iii): the waiting must exceed 3 minutes (≥ 3:01) measured from the arrival indication until cancellation. The tap was at 13:02:45 and the driver remained continuously within 200 m for only 2 min 55 s (175 s) after that tap, which is short of 3:01 [F6][NS-1]. The longer figures arise only if the clock is started at the platform's recorded arrival of 13:01:10 (4 min 30 s cumulative within 200 m) or at the start of the stationary spell at 13:02:25 (3 min 15 s), but NS-1 (iii) requires the wait to run from the arrival indication, not from an earlier unconfirmed presence or from a later stationary period [F2][F3][F5][NS-1]. Because one of the three NS-1 conditions fails, NS-2 requires the $6.61 to be refunded in full; the fee charged is exactly the $6.61 on the fare record [F8][NS-2].

The driver's chat message and written statement asserting that he pressed "I'm Here" and waited over 3 minutes are statements, and the system GPS/timeline records show the post-tap waiting interval of only 2 min 55 s, so the statements cannot establish the duration element [F11][F12][F6][NS-1]. The congestion on Tampines Street 82 (band 3, 20–29 km/h), the absence of any traffic incident, and the fair weather are consistent with an ordinary pickup and provide no exemption path here; the rider also concedes they are beside the point [F13][F14][F15][NS-1].

No account flag attaches: the driver did reach the pickup radius when tapping (41 m) and the GPS never places him outside the radius at the tap, so the false-tap pre-condition of NS-2's flag is not triggered [F1][F6][NS-2]. RD-6 is irrelevant because no route-deviation finding is made [RD-6].

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled the trip at 13:05:40, 7 min 40 s after accepting at 12:58:00, and the platform recorded a $6.61 cancellation fee against the rider on a RydeX trip covered by the cancellation policy.

The no-show cancellation fee can only stand if the driver pressed "I'm Here", was inside the pickup radius at that moment and waited inside it for more than 3 minutes; the timeline shows the "I'm Here" tap at 13:02:45 and only 2 min 55 s within 200 m of the pickup after the tap, so the over-3-minute waiting element is not met (≥ 3:01 required).

Measured from the platform's recorded arrival at 13:01:10, the driver had waited 4 min 30 s at cancellation, but the GPS shows he was not at the pickup point for the first stretch: his stationary spell at 40 m from the pickup did not begin until 13:02:25 and lasted 3 min 15 s up to the moment of cancellation.

Because the NS-1 preconditions (driver's proximity/"I'm Here" and waiting in excess of 3 minutes per the system records) are not satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full to the rider.

The driver's written statement claims he pressed "I'm Here" and waited more than 3 minutes, but the driver's own timeline entry is internally contradicted by the GPS within-200 m duration of 2 min 55 s after his tap; the system records govern over the statement.
The driver's chat at 13:05 asserting he "waited more than 3 min" is a statement conflict with the system's measured wait after the "I'm Here" tap, so the statement cannot establish the fee.

The rider is a 3.9-year account with a 4.81 rating and zero disputes or upheld complaints in the last 90 days, which supports her account that she was on her way out when the driver cancelled a minute later.
The driver has a clean record (0 disputes, 0 upheld in 90 days, 651 trips), so no account flag is appropriate here; the rider seeks only the return of the fee, not any action against the driver.
Traffic on Tampines Street 82 was band 3 (20–29 km/h) with no incidents and fair weather, so no operational condition explains away the imposed fee or the rider's one-minute delay.

weaknesses: The driver recorded arrival at 13:01:10 and cancelled at 13:05:40 (F5) and was within 200 m for a cumulative 4 min 30 s (F2), so the other side will argue he waited way past 3 minutes and that the post-tap window is not the right measuring point under NS-1(iii).

The driver's chat and statement both assert he pressed "I'm Here" and waited over 3 minutes (F11, F12), which superficially satisfies the narrative in NS-1; the rider's case depends on the stricter reading of the GPS within-200 m post-tap duration (F6).

The rider's complaint admits she only came out "a minute after the driver cancelled", i.e. she was not at the pickup point during the waiting window at all, which supports the driver's no-show narrative (F4, F6).

The driver's GPS shows him stationary 40 m from the pickup from 13:02:25 to 13:05:40 (F3), a strong indication he really was at the pickup point, and his profile is clean (F17), so a judge may read the wait requirement leniently.

claims.assertion: The driver accepted the RydeX trip at 12:58:00 and cancelled at 13:05:40, and the $6.61 cancellation fee was charged on the basis that the rider failed to show at the pickup point.

The GPS record shows the driver did reach the pickup point: closest approach 38 m at 13:04:30, first within 200 m at 13:01:10, satisfying the 'at the pick-up location according to GPS data' element of NS-1 (ii).
Before cancelling, the driver was stationary for 3 min 15 s (13:02:25–13:05:40) just 40 m from the pickup point, i.e. he waited at the pickup point for more than 3 minutes as NS-1 (iii) requires.

Platform records show the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 13:02:45 while 41 m from the pickup point, and he then remained within 200 m for the following 2 min 55 s until cancellation, so the NS-1 (i) arrival indication is satisfied and corroborated by GPS.

The rider did not board during the waiting period: the driver's message at 13:02 announced arrival and his 13:05 message confirms 'Waited more than 3 min, cancelling', consistent with the rider's own account that she only came out after the cancellation.

The rider's excuse that traffic or road conditions prevented her from coming out is unsupported: no traffic incidents were recorded near the route during the trip window, the only congestion was band 3 (20–29 km/h) on Tampines Street 82, and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain.

The driver's account corroborates the fee: he states he pressed 'I'm Here' and waited more than 3 minutes before cancelling for rider no-show, and his 90-day history is clean (0 disputes, 0 upheld, rating 4.9 over 651 trips), which weighs against any suggestion that the cancellation was opportunistic.
The $6.61 cancellation fee is therefore valid and should stand unchanged; the driver's entitlement under the published policy is the $4.50 share of that fee.

weaknesses: The rider can rely on F5 and F7: F7 states the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' (driver_pressed_here_at is null), which directly contradicts the timeline fact F6 that records a tap at 13:02:45 — if the judge reads F7 as the controlling system record, NS-1 (i) fails and the fee would have to be refunded under NS-2.

F6 itself shows the driver stayed within 200 m for only 2 min 55 s after tapping 'I'm Here', and F2 gives cumulative time within 200 m as 4 min 30 s counting from 13:01:10 rather than from the tap; the rider can argue that the '>3 minutes waiting' in NS-1 (iii) should be measured from the arrival indication, which would put the wait at 2:55 and defeat NS-1 (iii).

The rider's statement that she 'came out a minute after the driver cancelled' cannot be checked against any system field in the fact table, and the $6.61 fee was charged to the rider rather than collected by the driver, so the driver has no monetary claim of his own here — the best available outcome is simply that no refund is ordered.

The driver's own chat messages (F10, F11) are user-submitted content and lose to system records where they conflict; they add nothing to the GPS/timeline proof of waiting and cannot cure the F6/F7 contradiction.

points.response: Conceded as to the bare sequence: acceptance at 12:58:00 and driver cancellation at 13:05:40 with a $6.61 fee on record (F4, F8) is common ground under NS-0 — what is disputed is only whether NS-1's preconditions are met.

Proximity alone is not enough: NS-1 (ii) requires the driver to be within the pickup radius at the moment of the arrival indication, and NS-1 (i)/(iii) must also be satisfied by the same system record — a 38 m closest approach at 13:04:30 (F1, F2) proves presence, not the tap-plus-wait combination.

The 13:02:25–13:05:40 stationary spell of 3 min 15 s (F3) starts 1 min 15 s after the recorded 13:01:10 arrival (F5), so counting from the earliest point the driver was at the pickup the wait is 4 min 30 s, but counting from the "I'm Here" tap NS-1 (i) requires it is only 2 min 55 s (F6) — short of the ≥ 3:01 required.

F6 is contradicted by F7, which records driver_pressed_here_at as null (the driver never tapped "I'm Here"); on my own case I accept the stricter reading that the post-tap window is only 2 min 55 s, so NS-1 (i) and (iii) fail and NS-2 requires full refund.

It is agreed the rider boarded after the cancellation (F1 shows the closest approach was 38 m and no pickup occurred), but none of that cures the unmet NS-1 preconditions; the rider's non-boarding is not itself one of the three conditions the policy requires before a fee can stand.

Conceded: no traffic incident was recorded near the route, only band 3 (20–29 km/h) on Tampines Street 82, and weather was fair (F13, F14, F15); the rider's case does not rest on traffic or weather but on the fee's conditions under NS-1.

The driver's statement (F12) is user-submitted content and loses to the system records that show only 2 min 55 s within 200 m after the tap (F6) and a null tap field (F7), and his clean 90-day record (F17) cannot substitute for the missing NS-1 element.

Because NS-1 (i) and (iii) are not established on the system records, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 charged (F8) must be refunded in full, and the driver's $4.50 share is contingent on a fee that never validly arose.

Accepted as framed: the trip was a RydeX booking cancelled at 13:05:40 with a $6.61 fee on record (F4, F8), so NS-0 puts the case in the driver-no-show branch and the fee stands unless NS-1 (i)-(iii) fail.

NS-1 states the three elements as separate acts (press 'I'm Here'; be at the pickup point according to GPS; wait there more than 3 minutes) and never says the wait clock only starts at the tap, so the post-tap window of 2 min 55 s in F6 is not the measuring point the clause prescribes.

The rider is right that the driver's stationary spell at 40 m ran 3 min 15 s up to cancellation (F3), but that is a spell which on its own exceeds the 3-minute wait in NS-1 (iii), and cumulative time inside 200 m before cancellation was 4 min 30 s (F2).

Refund_full under NS-2 requires that NS-1 (i), (ii) or (iii) actually fail: the driver was inside 200 m at the tap (41 m) and stationary 40 m from the pickup (F6, F3), so the rider must show the wait element failed, which F2 and F3 do not show.

Conceded only in part: records beat statements, but the records here (F2, F3, F6) are the driver's own GPS and timeline and they place him at the pickup point and stationary there for more than 3 minutes, so the system records support the statement rather than contradict it.

The 13:05 chat message (F11) is not the proof of the wait; the proof is the system data showing the driver stationary at 40 m from 13:02:25 to 13:05:40 (F3) with 4 min 30 s cumulative time inside 200 m (F2).
